newsitem.title: USA: Clinton tosses pitch for education at ballpark.
newsitem.headline: Clinton tosses pitch for education at ballpark.

text.p: President Clinton made a pitch for excellence in education Wednesday, joining major league players in trying to convince kids to stay in school.

Before an inter-league game between the Baltimore Orioles and the Philadelphia Phillies, Clinton launched a public service campaign sponsored by Major League Baseball designed to stress the importance of education.

"Go back home and think what you can do to make sure that every one of our children is as devoted to excellence in education as the baseball players we'll enjoy watching today...are to excellence in their sport," Clinton told the crowd, standing at the pitcher's mound at Camden Yards.

Clinton met privately with players from both teams before the game. At one point, Philadelphia relief pitcher Ricky Bottalico and some teammates who view most games from the bench waited for Clinton clutching baseballs and pens.
When a reporter jokingly asked if they were going to offer the president their autographs, Bottalico replied: "He doesn't want ours. Have you ever seen any of us?
